work.title: Phantasiens Øe, eller "Fra Chinas Kyst", Første Akt
The Isle of Phantasy, or "From the Shore of China"
Original romantisk Ballet i 2 Acter og et Slutningstableau af August Bournonville
Original Romantic Ballet in Two Acts by August Bournonville

history.p:
In 1838 Bournonville contacted Hartmann asking him to write the music for his new ballet "Phantasiens Øe", which was to be performed on the birthday of queen Marie Sofie Frederikke on 28 October. It was probably the intention that Hartmann should have composed the complete music for the ballet, but when his father-in-law, the wealthy merchant Johann Friedrich Zinn, died on 21 September he had to pass on the job to Edvard Helsted, H.S. Paulli, Ivar Bredal, Ludvig Zinck and H.S..Løvenskiold. Hartmann had only managed to write / arrange Nos. 1-8 and 10-12. As it was custom at the time, Hartmann according to Knud Arne Jürgensen used several tunes by other composers:
No. 3, p. 62 (Mel: af Schulz) = "Matrosdands" from "Høstgildet".
No. 5, p. 108 (Mel: af d'Alayrac) unidentified and p. 181 (Motif by Schall) unidentified.
No. 8, p. 149 "Pas Russe" is based on the Russian song "Kalimuska".
No. 10, p. 195 is based on the famous Irish song "The Last Rose of Summer".
No. 11, p. 227 (Kong Christian etc.) = the Danish national anthem, possibly composed by Hartmann's grand father, Johann Hartmann.

physDesc.physMedium: In library binding with marbled sides and leather corners and spine with the monogram of King Christian X stamped in gold. No title page. Written in brown ink. Paper: 14 and 18 staves. Overture unpaginated, Nos. 1-4 consecutively paginated (bifolios only) 1-18 in upper right-hand corner. The inserted march by Du Puy unpaginated. At the bottom of each page later pagination in pencil 1-239. At the end of No. 4 on p. 87 Hartmann has written: "NB: Med den sidste Tact / indtræder Marchen af / Du Puy, bag Scenen." Page 88 blank, then follows an arrangement of Du Puy's march originally published in the music periodical "Nye Apollo", vol. 4 no. 1. This march is played on the stage. Above No. 8, the "Pas Russe", on p. 149: "Bournonville". No. 8 is in Edvard Helsted's hand and paginated each page. No. 9 is also in Helsted's hand and probably arranged by him. It is paginated on bifolios only 1-15. At the end of the music on p. 239, Hartmann signed and probably also dated his score, but this part of the paper has been torn out, so that only "Ende paa 1" and "I:P:E:H" is visible."
